modules.title: Foundation and Awareness
modules.description: Understand career readiness, personal strengths, values and transferable skills.

lessons.title: Understanding Career Readiness
lessons.content:
Understanding Career Readiness

Career readiness is more than getting a job. It combines self-awareness, communication, problem-solving, professionalism, digital confidence and the ability to take responsible action.

Learning Objectives

  • Explain what career readiness means.
  • Identify the main skills employers and learning institutions expect.
  • Recognize the difference between technical skills and transferable skills.

Key Ideas

  • Career readiness develops through practice, not only certificates.
  • Transferable skills such as communication, teamwork and problem-solving apply across many careers.
  • Knowing your current strengths and gaps helps you choose useful next steps.

Activity

Create a two-column list of your current strengths and the career-readiness skills you want to improve.
lessons.activity: Create a two-column list of your current strengths and the career-readiness skills you want to improve.

materials.title: Career Readiness Self-Assessment
materials.instructions: Rate yourself from 1 to 5 on communication, teamwork, problem-solving, digital confidence, professionalism and self-management. Write one improvement action for your two lowest areas.

lessons.title: Strengths, Interests and Values
lessons.content:
Strengths, Interests and Values

Good career decisions are stronger when they connect your abilities, interests and values to realistic opportunities.

Learning Objectives

  • Identify personal strengths and interests.
  • Describe values that matter in your future work.
  • Connect personal qualities to possible career areas.

Key Ideas

  • Strengths describe what you do well; interests describe what attracts your attention.
  • Values influence the kind of environment and work that feels meaningful.
  • A career choice should consider both personal fit and real-world opportunity.

Activity

Write your top five strengths, top three interests and top three work values. Identify two careers that could fit the combination.
lessons.activity: Write your top five strengths, top three interests and top three work values. Identify two careers that could fit the combination.

materials.title: Strengths and Career Fit Worksheet
materials.instructions: Complete the strengths, interests and values sections, then identify two possible career paths and explain why each one fits.

lessons.title: Transferable Skills and Evidence
lessons.content:
Transferable Skills and Evidence

Employers and schools value evidence. Learners need to explain not only which skills they have, but where and how they used them.

Learning Objectives

  • Identify transferable skills from school, volunteering, family responsibilities and projects.
  • Use a simple Situation-Action-Result structure to describe evidence.
  • Turn everyday experience into credible career examples.

Key Ideas

  • Unpaid experience can still demonstrate valuable skills.
  • Specific examples are stronger than vague claims.
  • Results can include improvement, completion, learning, service or problem resolution.

Activity

Write one Situation-Action-Result example that proves a skill you already have.
lessons.activity: Write one Situation-Action-Result example that proves a skill you already have.

materials.title: Transferable Skills Evidence Builder
materials.instructions: Choose three transferable skills and write one evidence example for each using Situation, Action and Result.

questions.question: Which statement best describes career readiness?
options: A combination of practical skills, self-awareness and professional behaviors
Having only a university degree
Applying for as many jobs as possible
Knowing one technical skill
questions.explanation: Career readiness combines practical skills, behaviors and the ability to apply them.

questions.question: Which is an example of a transferable skill?
options: Teamwork
A specific software license only
A company name
A job title
questions.explanation: Teamwork can transfer across many industries and roles.

questions.question: Why should you use evidence when describing a skill?
options: It makes the claim more credible
It guarantees employment
It replaces qualifications
It removes the need to practice
questions.explanation: Specific evidence helps demonstrate how you actually used the skill.

modules.title: Career Planning
modules.description: Explore pathways, set goals and build a practical career plan.

lessons.title: Exploring Career Pathways
lessons.content:
Exploring Career Pathways

Career planning starts with research. Learners should compare pathways rather than choosing based only on popularity, pressure or assumptions.

Learning Objectives

  • Research different career pathways.
  • Compare education, employment and entrepreneurship options.
  • Identify entry requirements and realistic first steps.

Key Ideas

  • The same interest can lead to several different careers.
  • Entry requirements vary by role, employer, sector and country.
  • Career plans should remain flexible as new information becomes available.

Activity

Choose one career area and research three possible roles within it. Record the main duties, skills, qualifications and entry routes.
lessons.activity: Choose one career area and research three possible roles within it. Record the main duties, skills, qualifications and entry routes.

materials.title: Career Pathway Research Sheet
materials.instructions: Research three related roles and compare duties, required skills, qualifications, likely entry routes and one source of reliable information for each.

lessons.title: Setting Career Goals
lessons.content:
Setting Career Goals

Career goals are useful when they translate ambition into measurable actions and deadlines.

Learning Objectives

  • Convert a broad career ambition into a specific goal.
  • Create short-term and medium-term career milestones.
  • Identify resources and support needed.

Key Ideas

  • A useful goal states what you will do and by when.
  • Large goals become easier when broken into smaller milestones.
  • Reviewing progress regularly helps you adjust without abandoning the overall direction.

Activity

Write one 90-day career goal and break it into three 30-day milestones.
lessons.activity: Write one 90-day career goal and break it into three 30-day milestones.

materials.title: Career Goal Planner
materials.instructions: Create one 90-day goal, three milestones, the support/resources needed, and evidence that will show each milestone is complete.

lessons.title: Building Your Career Plan
lessons.content:
Building Your Career Plan

A career plan should connect your target, current position, gaps and actions in one practical document.

Learning Objectives

  • Identify the gap between current readiness and target requirements.
  • Prioritize the most important development actions.
  • Create a simple plan that can be reviewed monthly.

Key Ideas

  • Not every skill gap needs to be solved immediately.
  • Priority should be based on relevance and impact.
  • A career plan is a living document and should change as circumstances change.

Activity

Create a one-page career plan covering target role, current strengths, gaps, actions, deadlines and support required.
lessons.activity: Create a one-page career plan covering target role, current strengths, gaps, actions, deadlines and support required.

materials.title: One-Page Career Plan
materials.instructions: Complete the target role, current strengths, top gaps, three priority actions, deadlines and people/resources that can support you.

questions.question: What is the best first step when exploring a career?
options: Research roles, requirements and pathways
Choose the highest-paying title without research
Copy another person's plan
Wait until graduation
questions.explanation: Research helps you make realistic and informed decisions.

questions.question: A useful career goal should be:
options: Specific and time-bound
Very broad with no deadline
Based only on what others want
Impossible to measure
questions.explanation: Specific, measurable goals make progress easier to manage.

questions.question: What should a career plan include?
options: Target, gaps, actions and deadlines
Only the target job title
Only qualifications already completed
Only salary expectations
questions.explanation: A practical plan connects the target to current gaps and next actions.

modules.title: Practice and Application
modules.description: Develop a strong CV or resume, professional profile and tailored applications.

lessons.title: Creating a Strong CV or Resume
lessons.content:
Creating a Strong CV or Resume

A CV or resume should make it easy for the reader to understand your relevant skills, experience, achievements and potential.

Learning Objectives

  • Identify the essential sections of a CV or resume.
  • Write clear achievement-focused bullet points.
  • Tailor content to a specific opportunity.

Key Ideas

  • Relevance is more important than including everything you have ever done.
  • Action verbs and specific results make experience stronger.
  • Formatting should be clear, consistent and easy to scan.

Activity

Draft or improve one CV section using action verbs and evidence of results.
lessons.activity: Draft or improve one CV section using action verbs and evidence of results.

materials.title: CV Improvement Checklist
materials.instructions: Review your CV for contact details, profile, education, experience, skills, achievements, consistency, spelling and relevance to your target role.

lessons.title: Professional Profile and Online Presence
lessons.content:
Professional Profile and Online Presence

Your professional profile helps employers, schools, partners and collaborators quickly understand who you are and what value you can offer.

Learning Objectives

  • Write a concise professional summary.
  • Identify appropriate information for a professional online profile.
  • Recognize digital behaviors that can affect professional reputation.

Key Ideas

  • A strong profile is specific about skills, interests and direction.
  • Online activity can contribute to professional credibility or undermine it.
  • Consistency across your CV, applications and profiles builds trust.

Activity

Write a 60- to 90-word professional summary for your CV or online profile.
lessons.activity: Write a 60- to 90-word professional summary for your CV or online profile.

materials.title: Professional Profile Builder
materials.instructions: Write a headline, short summary, five skills and two examples of work, volunteering, projects or learning that support your target.

lessons.title: Applications and Cover Messages
lessons.content:
Applications and Cover Messages

Applications are stronger when they show clear alignment between the opportunity and the learner's evidence.

Learning Objectives

  • Read an opportunity description for requirements and priorities.
  • Match relevant evidence to the requirement.
  • Write a concise cover message or application introduction.

Key Ideas

  • Generic applications are weaker than tailored ones.
  • Use the language of the opportunity where it accurately reflects your experience.
  • A short, relevant message is usually stronger than an unfocused long one.

Activity

Choose a real or sample opportunity and write a 120-word tailored application message.
lessons.activity: Choose a real or sample opportunity and write a 120-word tailored application message.

materials.title: Application Matching Worksheet
materials.instructions: List five requirements from an opportunity and match each to one piece of evidence from your experience, projects, education or volunteering.

questions.question: What makes a CV bullet stronger?
options: A clear action plus evidence or result
Using many unrelated adjectives
Writing one very long paragraph
Including every activity regardless of relevance
questions.explanation: Action and evidence help the reader understand your contribution.

questions.question: What should a professional summary communicate?
options: Relevant strengths, direction and value
Private personal information
Every subject you have ever studied
Only your age
questions.explanation: A concise professional summary should show relevant strengths and direction.

questions.question: Why should an application be tailored?
options: To connect your evidence to the specific requirements
To make it longer
To avoid reading the opportunity
To guarantee selection
questions.explanation: Tailoring demonstrates relevance; it does not guarantee selection.

modules.title: Professional Readiness
modules.description: Prepare for interviews, communicate professionally and demonstrate workplace readiness.

lessons.title: Interview Preparation
lessons.content:
Interview Preparation

Interview preparation reduces avoidable uncertainty and helps learners communicate evidence clearly.

Learning Objectives

  • Research the role and organization before an interview.
  • Prepare examples for common competency questions.
  • Use Situation-Task-Action-Result to structure answers.

Key Ideas

  • Preparation should focus on relevant examples, not memorizing a script word-for-word.
  • Strong answers explain what you personally did.
  • Questions for the interviewer can demonstrate preparation and curiosity.

Activity

Prepare three STAR examples: one for teamwork, one for problem-solving and one for handling a challenge.
lessons.activity: Prepare three STAR examples: one for teamwork, one for problem-solving and one for handling a challenge.

materials.title: Interview STAR Practice Sheet
materials.instructions: Write Situation, Task, Action and Result for three examples. Keep each example focused on your own actions and outcome.

lessons.title: Professional Communication
lessons.content:
Professional Communication

Professional communication includes clear speaking, respectful writing, active listening and appropriate follow-up.

Learning Objectives

  • Use clear and respectful workplace communication.
  • Write a concise professional email or message.
  • Practice active listening and clarification.

Key Ideas

  • Professional communication is clear, purposeful and respectful.
  • Tone matters in email, messaging, meetings and interviews.
  • Confirming expectations can prevent avoidable mistakes.

Activity

Write a professional follow-up message after a mock interview or networking conversation.
lessons.activity: Write a professional follow-up message after a mock interview or networking conversation.

materials.title: Professional Communication Practice
materials.instructions: Draft a subject line and short professional message that thanks the recipient, refers to the conversation and states an appropriate next step.

lessons.title: Workplace Readiness and Professionalism
lessons.content:
Workplace Readiness and Professionalism

Professionalism is demonstrated through reliability, responsibility, ethical behavior, teamwork and willingness to learn.

Learning Objectives

  • Recognize behaviors associated with workplace professionalism.
  • Explain how reliability and accountability build trust.
  • Identify appropriate responses to common workplace situations.

Key Ideas

  • Professionalism applies in physical, remote and hybrid environments.
  • Owning mistakes and communicating early is usually better than hiding problems.
  • Respect, boundaries and confidentiality matter in professional environments.

Activity

Review three workplace scenarios and write the most professional response to each.
lessons.activity: Review three workplace scenarios and write the most professional response to each.

materials.title: Workplace Readiness Scenario Sheet
materials.instructions: Respond to scenarios involving a missed deadline, disagreement with a teammate and unclear instructions. Explain why your response is professional.

questions.question: What is a strong way to structure a competency interview example?
options: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Title, Salary, Address, Reference
Problem, Blame, Excuse, Exit
Question, Silence, Guess, Finish
questions.explanation: STAR helps organize evidence clearly.

questions.question: What is an example of professional communication?
options: A clear, respectful message with an appropriate next step
Ignoring a request indefinitely
Sending confidential information publicly
Using an aggressive tone
questions.explanation: Professional communication should be clear, respectful and purposeful.

questions.question: If you realize you may miss a deadline, the best first response is usually to:
options: Communicate early, explain the risk and propose a next step
Hide the problem
Blame a teammate immediately
Stop responding
questions.explanation: Early communication and accountability protect trust and help resolve issues.

modules.title: Action, Reflection and Reporting
modules.description: Build professional relationships, execute a 30-day action plan and create evidence of progress.

lessons.title: Networking and Opportunity Building
lessons.content:
Networking and Opportunity Building

Networking is the process of building genuine professional relationships and learning from people, communities and opportunities.

Learning Objectives

  • Explain networking as relationship-building rather than asking strangers for jobs.
  • Prepare a concise introduction.
  • Identify safe and relevant places to build professional connections.

Key Ideas

  • Good networking is reciprocal and respectful.
  • A short introduction should communicate who you are, your interest and the reason for connecting.
  • Following up appropriately helps turn a first conversation into a professional relationship.

Activity

Write a 30-second professional introduction and identify five people or communities you can learn from.
lessons.activity: Write a 30-second professional introduction and identify five people or communities you can learn from.

materials.title: Networking Action Sheet
materials.instructions: Create your introduction, list five target connections or communities, and write one respectful outreach message.

lessons.title: Your 30-Day Career Action Plan
lessons.content:
Your 30-Day Career Action Plan

Progress depends on converting learning into repeated action. A short action plan creates accountability and evidence of movement.

Learning Objectives

  • Prioritize the next three career actions.
  • Set measurable weekly commitments.
  • Define evidence of progress.

Key Ideas

  • Small consistent actions are more sustainable than occasional intense effort.
  • Track applications, learning, networking and portfolio progress.
  • Review what works and adapt your plan.

Activity

Create a 30-day plan with weekly actions for learning, applications/opportunities, networking and portfolio development.
lessons.activity: Create a 30-day plan with weekly actions for learning, applications/opportunities, networking and portfolio development.

materials.title: 30-Day Career Action Plan
materials.instructions: Plan four weeks of specific actions. Include target dates, evidence of completion and a weekly review question.

lessons.title: Reflection, Portfolio and Next Steps
lessons.content:
Reflection, Portfolio and Next Steps

Career readiness improves when learners collect evidence of learning and reflect on how their skills have developed.

Learning Objectives

  • Review progress across the course outcomes.
  • Identify evidence to include in a simple career portfolio.
  • Choose next steps based on current readiness.

Key Ideas

  • A portfolio can include projects, certificates, writing samples, presentations, volunteer evidence and reflections.
  • Reflection helps convert experience into stronger future performance.
  • Career development continues after the course.

Activity

Create a simple portfolio checklist and write a final reflection describing three skills you improved and your next three actions.
lessons.activity: Create a simple portfolio checklist and write a final reflection describing three skills you improved and your next three actions.

materials.title: Career Readiness Final Reflection
materials.instructions: List evidence you can include in your portfolio, rate yourself again on the original self-assessment areas, and write your next three career actions.

questions.question: What is the best description of networking?
options: Building genuine professional relationships and learning from others
Asking every new contact for a job immediately
Collecting as many names as possible
Only attending large events
questions.explanation: Networking is relationship-building, not simply requesting jobs.

questions.question: A useful 30-day action plan should contain:
options: Specific actions, dates and evidence of completion
Only a long-term dream
No deadlines
Actions controlled entirely by other people
questions.explanation: Specific actions and evidence make progress trackable.

questions.question: Why is a career portfolio useful?
options: It provides evidence of skills, learning and completed work
It replaces all interviews
It guarantees a job
It should contain only certificates
questions.explanation: A portfolio helps demonstrate capability with concrete evidence.

questions.question: Which approach best demonstrates career readiness?
options: Combining self-awareness, practical skills, evidence and consistent action
Waiting for opportunities without preparation
Focusing only on qualifications
Using the same generic application everywhere
questions.explanation: Career readiness is demonstrated through practical capability, evidence and action.

questions.question: What is the strongest way to show an employer that you have a skill?
options: Give a specific example showing what you did and the result
Simply say you are excellent
List the skill repeatedly
Avoid discussing experience
questions.explanation: Evidence-based examples make skill claims credible.

questions.question: When researching a career path, what should you compare?
options: Role duties, skills, entry requirements and realistic pathways
Only the job title
Only social media popularity
Only one person's opinion
questions.explanation: Good career decisions use multiple pieces of reliable information.

questions.question: Why should a CV or resume be tailored?
options: To emphasize evidence relevant to the specific opportunity
To make every application identical
To include unrelated information
To avoid reading the role description
questions.explanation: Tailoring improves relevance.

questions.question: What does STAR stand for in interview preparation?
options: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Skill, Title, Application, Reference
Study, Test, Answer, Review
Summary, Target, Achievement, Resume
questions.explanation: STAR is a standard structure for communicating experience clearly.

questions.question: Which behavior demonstrates professionalism?
options: Communicating early about risks and taking responsibility
Ignoring unclear instructions
Sharing confidential information
Blaming others before investigating
questions.explanation: Responsibility and early communication help build trust.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 30-day career action plan?
options: Turn career goals into specific, trackable actions
Guarantee a job within 30 days
Replace career research
Avoid reviewing progress
questions.explanation: A short action plan turns goals into measurable action.

questions.question: Which item can be part of a career portfolio?
options: Projects and work samples
Only a birth certificate
Only social media followers
Nothing until you are employed
questions.explanation: Projects and work samples are useful evidence of capability.

questions.question: What is a healthy approach to networking?
options: Build respectful relationships and learn from others
Ask every person for money or a job
Contact people repeatedly after they decline
Pretend to have experience you do not have
questions.explanation: Professional networking should be genuine and respectful.

questions.question: After completing the course, what is the best next step?
options: Apply the learning, track progress and continue developing gaps
Stop learning completely
Wait for someone else to create a career plan
Use one generic CV forever
questions.explanation: Career development is continuous and improves through action and review.
